column3: Run synthetic benchmark in precomputed mode
column4:
Start local backend services.

Open a terminal in the project root.

Run the CLI with `run`, backend `qdrant`, embedding mode `precomputed`, a valid synthetic workload, and a small document count.

Wait for the command to finish and inspect the generated run folder.
column5:
The benchmark should complete without runtime errors.

The run folder should contain `trace.jsonl`, `metrics.csv`, `summary.json`, and `report.html`.

The summary should record freshness-related metrics and document counts.
column6:
Synthetic precomputed execution completes successfully in the local benchmark environment.

Expected artifacts are generated under the run output directory and summary metrics are populated.
column8: Validates the primary single-run workflow and artifact generation path.

column4:
Configure a valid embedding API key in the environment.

Run the CLI with `run`, backend `weaviate` or `qdrant`, embedding mode `live`, and a supported embedding model.

Wait for completion and inspect the generated artifacts.
column5:
The benchmark should complete and record embedding latency in addition to backend timing.

Artifacts should be generated in the output directory.

The summary should include embedding source metadata.
column6:
Live-mode flow is functionally supported and produces the expected artifact set in a configured environment.

Embedding latency is captured as part of the end-to-end measurement.
column8: This case depends on valid credentials and outbound connectivity.

column4:
Prepare a valid JSONL dataset or text directory.

Run the CLI with workload `dataset`, a correct dataset path, a valid dataset format, and the required text field.

Inspect summary and trace outputs after completion.
column5:
The benchmark should load dataset documents, inject deterministic retrieval anchors into indexed text, and complete successfully.

Dataset metadata should appear in `summary.json`.

Trace records should retain source references.
column6: Dataset-backed execution is supported and records dataset configuration and source references in generated artifacts.
column8: The implementation supports `jsonl` and `text-dir` dataset formats.

column4:
Start local backends.

Run the CLI with `compare`, multiple backends, at least one rate, and one embedding mode.

Wait for all runs to finish and inspect the comparison output folder.
column5:
The system should execute each expanded run combination.

The comparison output directory should contain `comparison.json`, `comparison.csv`, and `comparison.html`.

Nested run folders should also be present.
column6: Comparison workflow generates combined artifacts and linked per-run outputs as designed.
column8: Confirms matrix expansion across backend and rate combinations.

column4:
Start required local services.

Run the CLI with `pack` using the default preset set or a selected preset list.

Wait for trial execution to complete and inspect the pack output directory.
column5:
The system should execute repeated comparison trials for each preset.

The output directory should contain `benchmark_pack.json`, `benchmark_pack.csv`, and `benchmark_pack.html`.

Preset trial folders should exist under `presets/`.
column6: Pinned preset execution and aggregated pack reporting are implemented and generate the expected outputs.
column8: This covers the review-oriented benchmark-pack workflow.

column3: Regenerate an HTML report from existing artifacts
column4:
Complete at least one benchmark run.

Run the CLI with `report` and point it to an existing run directory, or allow it to discover the latest run.

Open the regenerated HTML file.
column5:
The report command should rebuild `report.html` from stored run artifacts without rerunning the benchmark.

The generated file should be readable in a browser.
column6: Report regeneration works as intended and supports review refreshes after a prior run.
column8: Useful when report styling or packaging is updated after execution.

column4:
Run the CLI with workload `dataset` but omit `dataset_path`, `dataset_format`, or `text_field`, or provide a missing file path.

Observe the CLI response.
column5:
The CLI should fail fast with a validation error.

No misleading success message or partial benchmark result should be produced.
column6: Validation rejects malformed dataset configurations and surfaces an explicit error path.
column8: Confirms defensive validation in configuration handling.

column4:
Run the CLI separately for `qdrant`, `weaviate`, and `pgvector` using valid local endpoints.

For pgvector, also verify behavior when DSN is absent or incorrect.
column5:
Each supported backend should initialize through its adapter and participate in benchmark execution when configured correctly.

Missing mandatory backend configuration should produce an error.
column6:
Backend selection and adapter routing are working for the intended local setup.

Error handling for invalid pgvector configuration is present.
column8: Confirms adapter contract usage and backend-specific validation.

column4:
Execute a benchmark run and open `metrics.csv` and `summary.json`.

Check document totals, success counts, rates, and latency fields for internal consistency.

Confirm that HTML output corresponds to the underlying artifact data.
column5:
Artifact files should agree on run identity, document counts, and major metrics.

HTML output should reflect the stored summary and metrics data.
column6: Artifacts are internally coherent in sampled review runs. Minor formatting polish remains for reviewer-facing presentation.
column8: Final review pass should include one more formatting sweep on generated HTML.

column4:
Open the generated HTML reports and review documents.

Check wording consistency, formatting, and naming alignment across outputs.

Capture any remaining refinements.
column5: Reviewer-facing material should be consistent, polished, and presentation-ready.
column6: Core content is complete, but a small final wording and layout pass is still pending before final submission.
column8: This is intentionally marked pending because the project is in the final polishing stage.
